US Legal Forms

If you are researching the mechanics of a debt covenant itself, the fundamental principles governing these agreements are detailed below.
What is a Debt Covenant?
A debt covenant is a binding clause or legal restriction embedded in a loan or bond agreement. Lenders implement them to mitigate risk and safeguard their capital by ensuring the borrower maintains operational stability and financial health throughout the life of the loan. 
insightsoftware
 +2
The Three Core Types of Debt Covenants
Debt covenants are generally grouped into three separate categories based on their requirements:
Affirmative (Positive) Covenants: Actions the borrower must take. Examples include submitting regular audited financial statements, maintaining proper business insurance, and paying corporate taxes on time. 
eCapital
 +4
Negative (Restrictive) Covenants: Actions the borrower cannot take without explicit lender approval. These usually restrict taking on additional debt, issuing massive shareholder dividends, or selling off major company assets. 
Wall Street Prep
 +4
Financial Covenants: Specific metrics and accounting ratios the borrower must maintain. They are continuously monitored or evaluated at the close of every quarter. 
Grant Thornton International
 +3
Common Financial Ratios Maintained
Lenders analyze corporate risk using standard liquidity and leverage thresholds: 
Carta
 +1
Covenant Metric	What it Measures	Formula / Indicator
Debt-to-EBITDA	Overall leverage and debt-clearing timeline	Total Debt / EBITDA
Interest Coverage Ratio	Ability to pay interest on outstanding debt	Operating Income (EBIT) / Interest Expense
Debt Service Coverage (DSCR)	Cash flow availability to cover principal + interest	Net Operating Income / Total Debt Service
Current Ratio	Short-term liquidity and operational health	Current Assets / Current Liabilities
Consequences of a Covenant Breach
Failing to meet a covenant threshold results in a "technical default". If a breach occurs, the debt is classified as current on the balance sheet, and the lender holds legal leverage to execute several penalties: 
CPA Hall Talk
 +3
Accelerating the loan to demand immediate, full repayment
Increasing the loan's predetermined interest rate
Demanding additional corporate asset collateral
Charging

Interest Coverage Ratio	Ability to pay interest on outstanding debt	Operating Income (EBIT) / Interest Expense
Debt Service Coverage (DSCR)	Cash flow availability to cover principal + interest	Net Operating Income / Total Debt Service
Current Ratio	Short-term liquidity and operational health	Current Assets / Current Liabilities
Consequences of a Covenant Breach
Failing to meet a covenant threshold results in a "technical default". If a breach occurs, the debt is classified as current on the balance sheet, and the lender holds legal leverage to execute several penalties: 
CPA Hall Talk
 +3
Accelerating the loan to demand immediate, full repayment
Increasing the loan's predetermined interest rate
Demanding additional corporate asset collateral
Charging
